summary: Iteration 20 — tested the four P2 features (A trending strip, B admin members filter, C preview DB reset, D ToS stamping) plus G hashtag regression. 21/21 backend pytest cases pass; all targeted frontend selectors render and behave correctly across /, /members (admin + non-admin), /apply, /admin (Orphans tab), and /tag/{tag}.

integration_issues.issue: Clicking a trending chip (count >= 2) sometimes yields '0 of 50 items' in the river. The trending endpoint scans up to 2000 titles in the configured hours window, while the river only paginates 50 items at a time, so a topic counted across the broader window can produce a 0-match in-memory filter unless the user scrolls/loads more. UX-wise the empty-state copy is correct ('No headlines in the last 48h match "..."') but is potentially confusing. Consider either (a) auto-paginating to find matches, (b) using article_indices from the API to highlight matching items, or (c) showing the chip count alongside the active-filter banner so users see the discrepancy is expected.

action_items: (Optional UX) Reconcile trending chip count with river filter coverage — see integration_issues above.
(Optional UX) tag-page-popular is not rendered when DB has zero posts; if main agent wants the strip always visible (per task description), guard with an empty-but-visible state.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/admin_reset.py: AGG_ALLOW_DB_RESET defaults to 'true' if unset — this means /reset is ENABLED on any environment that doesn't explicitly disable it, including potentially production. Recommend defaulting to 'false' and requiring opt-in on preview only.

routes/admin_reset.py: the /reset endpoint preserves admin-authored posts via $nin: admin_user_ids but the comment on line 109-111 says replies are wiped by author — admin replies will be preserved by the same $nin guard which is good, but the inline comment is slightly misleading ('any reply by a non-admin user' wipes — correct, but worth clarifying).

routes/applications.py: the rate-limit (max 1 application per 24h per email, line 70-75) runs AFTER the tos_accepted check and AFTER the 'already approved' early return but BEFORE invite-code redemption. Good ordering for the iter20 feature, but note that a user without tos_accepted always gets 400 even if rate-limited — that's correct.

services/trending.py: compute_trending iterates trigrams.most_common() with a 'break' on count < 2 which is fine for Counter ordering, but if the limit is small and trigrams dominate, bigrams are skipped entirely. Verified working in this run (8 chips returned, mix of bigrams). Behavior matches PRD.

routes/users.py: GET /api/members re-fetches every approved user + profile on every request with no pagination cursor (limit applied AFTER filter). At >2000 members this will hit the to_list(2000) cap. Acceptable for current scale but worth noting.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all expected data-testid selectors found and behaviors verified)

Cleaned up after the module. Frontend run also seeds an admin/member/applicant pair which is removed at the end. context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter20 added /api/agg/trending, /api/admin/preview-db/preview + /reset, /api/applications/tos-version + tos_accepted gate, /api/members?filter=. The reset endpoint is destructive — pytest module test_iter20_p2_features::TestResetDB runs LAST and DOES execute the real reset (preserved aggregator publishers=28, articles=585, substack imports=20 in this env). Re-runs of the suite are safe because the seed fixture re-creates everything; however any other test data on the DB at the time will be wiped. AGG_ALLOW_DB_RESET defaults to 'true' so the endpoint is reachable in this preview env. ToS PDF hash on this env is 9063ca44b62a... (full sha256 64 chars).
